title: Iowa HHS — IHAWP community engagement requirements
added: Official State of Iowa Website Agencies A-Z Programs & Services Health & Human Services IHAWP Community Engagement Requirements On this page...

About How to Meet New Requirements Exclusions Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) Resources Back to top About By December 1, 2026, certain Iowa Health and Wellness Plan (IHWAP) members must meet monthly requirements to enroll and maintain coverage.

Back to top How to Meet New Requirements There are several ways to meet these new requirements, including working, participating in an education or work program, completing community service, or combining different activities.

List items for IHAWP Work Requirement Activities You must either: Work at least 80 hours per month, or Earn at least $580 per month based on the federal minimum wage.\ Work can be: Paid work Work in exchange for goods or services (in-kind work) Unpaid work Seasonal workers: Income is averaged over six months.
Enroll in a qualifying job training or work program for 80+ hours per month.
Enrolling in an education program at least half-time meets work requirements.

Education programs include: High school GED program at a community college Community college Vocational and technical school 4-year colleges and universities leading to a bachelor's degree 1-2 year programs leading to a master's or higher-level degree Community service through unpaid work with a structured program completed for the benefit of the community meets work requirement activities.

Examples of community service locations: Schools Humane society Libraries Food banks Park volunteer You can meet the requirement by completing a combination of activities totaling at least 80 hours per month, including: Work Education or training Work programs Community service Back to top Exclusions Some people on the IHAWP program are excluded from these new requirements.

These groups include: American Indians/Alaska Natives Those under 19 or over 64 Individuals who are medically frail or otherwise have special medical needs + NOTE: The state may require medical documentation for the medically frail exclusion.

Pregnant or had a baby in the last 12 months while on Iowa Medicaid Caregivers of children under 14 or someone with a disability Participating in a drug or alcohol treatment program Participants in SNAP or FIP work programs Veterans rated as totally disabled Individuals currently or recently in jail or prison Back to top Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) List items for Community Engagement Requirements FAQ Download a digital or print-friendly (153.32 KB) .pdf version of the FAQ.

If the requirement applies to you, you must spend at least 80 hours each month on one or more of these activities: Work:Work for 80 hours per month or earn at least $580 per month (based on federal minimum wage).\ Income from seasonal work may be averaged over six months.
Job Training:Take part in a qualifying job training or work program for 80 hours per month.
Education:Enrolled in a high school, college, GED, or other career and technical programs at least half-time.
Community Service:Volunteer work for 80 hours per month.
You can combine different activities to reach your 80 hours.
Note: New applicants must meet CER for the month prior to the month of their application.
Current members must meet CER for at least two months since their last Medicaid application or renewal.

Pregnant or had a baby in the last 12 months while on Iowa Medicaid Caregivers of children under 14 or someone with a disability Participating in a drug or alcohol treatment program Participants in SNAP or FIP work programs Veterans rated as totally disabled Individuals currently or recently in jail or prison Update your contact information.
Make sure Iowa HHS has your current information (like address, phone number, and email address) so they can contact you about these eligibility changes.
Check your mail and email.
Iowa HHS will send you a letter or email in the upcoming months if the eligibility changes apply to you.
Keep track of, or gather documents for, any work, volunteer, job training, or school hours you complete each month.
Iowa HHS will contact you when this information is required.

To report a change call 1-877-347-5678 or by emailing [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#e5aca8a6b6a6a58d8d96cb8c8a9284cb828a93) If you want to see whether these requirements apply to you, visit our Self-Service Portal and chat with Ellie, our virtual assistant.

To report a change call 1-877-347-5678 or by emailing [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#632a2e203020230b0b104d0a0c14024d040c15) Participants can meet the community engagement requirements by completing approved volunteer hours.

summary.headline: Updated formatting and added specific details to IHAWP community engagement requirements page.
details: Reorganized content structure with clearer section headers and 'Back to top' links.
Clarified work requirement options to include earning at least $580 per month based on federal minimum wage, in addition to 80 hours of work.
Added specific examples of qualifying education programs (e.g., GED, community college, vocational school, 4-year universities).
Specified examples of qualifying community service locations (schools, humane society, libraries, food banks, park volunteer).
Added detailed FAQ guidance: new applicants must meet requirements for the month prior to application; current members must meet for at least two months since last Medicaid application or renewal.
Included actionable steps for members: update contact information, check mail/email, track hours/gather documents.
Expanded resources section with links to flyers, public resource directory, volunteer opportunities, job help, and member letters (including Spanish).
Added note that state may require medical documentation for medically frail exclusion.
summary.who_is_affected: Certain Iowa Health and Wellness Plan (IHWAP) members who are subject to monthly community engagement requirements to maintain eligibility.
summary.navigator_action: Review updated requirements with members, especially the $580/month income alternative and two-month look-back for current members; assist with tracking hours and updating contact information; direct members to new FAQ PDF and self-service portal.

Goals Improve health, well-being, and financial stability Help people become more independent and rely less on government support Increase workforce participation and improve job skills Use public resources responsibly and increase personal responsibility Key changes include More frequent check-ins will help confirm that members still qualify for coverage.
Many adults enrolled in Medicaid Expansion may need to meet the community engagement requirement through qualifying activities such as work, education, volunteer service, or job training.
Some individuals may be excluded due to age, health, or other status.
Updated forms and verification processes help confirm community engagement activities, exclusions, and other eligibility information when needed.
Keep Contact Information Current To keep coverage active, Medicaid members should carefully read all mail and keep their contact information up to date.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Eligibility Requirements To be eligible for Medicaid Expansion, you must show one of the following: You are meeting the community engagement requirement or You qualify for an exclusion to the community engagement requirement Eligibility and compliance are verified during the initial application process and during the redetermination process.

How to Apply Online (Self-Service Portal) Apply online at apply.mt.gov Paper Application (Mail or in Person) By mail: Human and Community Services Division PO Box 202925 Helena, MT 59602-2925 In person at a local eligibility office, also known as an Office of Public Assistance or OPA \Note: Supporting documentation and appendices are optional at the time of application.

By Phone Call the Public Assistance Helpline (PAHL) at 1-888-706-1535 Community Engagement Requirement Flyer Exclusion Information Flyer Verification Matrix Self-Service Portal Navigation Guide Medically Frail Guidance Montana Medicaid: Presumptive Eligibility (PE) for Community Engagement Community Engagement Reporting Forms + Appendix A: Medicaid Community Engagement Activity Requirements Reporting Form + Application Appendix B: Community Engagement Exclusions Form + Redetermination Appendix B: Community Engagement Exclusions Form Overview Some individuals enrolled in Medicaid Expansion must meet the monthly community engagement requirement unless they are a specified excluded individual.

Qualifying Activities Qualifying activities include: Working at a job (paid or in-kind), demonstrated by income of at least $580 per month or docmentation of 80 hours of work if income cannot be verified Community service or volunteering with a not-for-profit organization Participating in an approved state or federal workforce training or job readiness program Doing an internship or apprenticeship Going to school at least half time Combining activities (for example, you could work 60 hours and complete 20 hours of community service) Verification You must prove you are meeting this requirement.

Examples of documentation, if requested by DPHHS, may include: Pay stubs from your job Official letters from your school Signed volunteer logs showing your hours Other documentation requested by DPHHS You must continue meeting the requirement throughout your coverage.

Your completion of community engagement activities may be verified through: Existing electronic data sources or data matching with other state programs, and/or Self-reporting online, by phone, by mail, or in person using approved methods Additional supporting documentation, if requested by DPHHS At the time of application, the community engagement requirement forms (Appendix A and B) and supporting documentation are optional.

Community Engagement Exclusions When applying or renewing coverage, you must demonstrate that you meet the community engagement requirement unless you qualify for an exclusion: At application: The month before your new application At redetermination: At least 3 months since your last redetermination (the months do not need to be consecutive) If you believe you may qualify for a Medically Frail exclusion, visit the Medically Frail Guidance for additional guidance.
Exceptions and short-term hardships temporarily satisfy the requirement for the months they apply: If you are a specified excluded individual, the requirement does not apply to you at all.
If you have an exception or a short-term hardship, you are treated as meeting the requirement only for the months that the exception or hardship applies to you.

At redetermination, if you cannot show that you had an exception or short-term hardship for three of the months since your last redetermination, you will need to meet the community engagement requirement through approved activities to keep your Medicaid coverage.
Specified Exclusions apply to your current situation.

You may be excluded if one or more of the following options apply to you at the time of your application or redetermination: American Indian/Alaska Native Former Foster Youth under age 26 who were on Medicaid and in foster care when they turned 18 Inmate of a public institution (e.g., jail, prison) People with a medical condition or health needs that impact their ability to work or do other community engagement activities (for more information on this exclusion, please reference the Medically Frail webpage) Parent, guardian, caretaker relative, or family caregiver of a dependent child under age 14 or a disabled individual People in a drug or alcohol rehabilitation or treatment program People who meet TANF work requirements, or receive SNAP and are subject to SNAP work requirements Women who are pregnant or postpartum (up to 12 months) Veterans with a total (100%) disability rating Exceptions and short-term hardships may fulfill part or all of the community engagement requirement for the months that they apply to you: Children aged 18 or younger People entitled to or enrolled in Medicare Part A or Part B People eligible for Medicaid for any other eligibility group People incarcerated in the last three months People who are specified excluded individuals during part of their lookback period People experiencing the following short-term hardships: + Receiving inpatient services + Residing in a county with an emergency disaster declaration (Note: Montana will automatically apply this for clients if a disaster is declared) + Residing in a county with high unemployment (Note: Montana will not be implementing the high unemployment exception at this time, and will automatically apply this for clients if enacted in the future) + Person or dependent who must travel outside of their community for medical services for a serious or complex medical condition At application, you must show that the exception or hardship applied for the month before your new application.
At redetermination, you must show that the exception or hardship applied for at least 3 months since your last redetermination.
The months do not need to be consecutive.
If you have an exception for only one or two months, you must complete the remainder of the community engagement requirement by reporting qualifying activity hours.
1 also changes retroactive coverage for the Medicaid Expansion population from 3 months to 1 month, effective January 1, 2027.
For people in other eligibility groups, retroactive coverage will change from 3 months to 2 months.
Individuals must still request retroactive coverage.
Additionally, individuals must meet all eligibility requirements for the retroactive period.

summary.headline: Montana removed detailed Medicaid expansion content including specific requirements, examples, forms, and webinar links while keeping core structure.
details: Removed detailed eligibility requirements for Medicaid Expansion including specific criteria like meeting community engagement or qualifying for exclusion.
Removed comprehensive information about qualifying activities for community engagement such as work hours, volunteering, education, and combinations.
Removed specific documentation examples like pay stubs, school letters, and volunteer logs for verifying community engagement.
Removed detailed explanations of verification methods including electronic data matching and self-reporting options.

Removed extensive lists of specified exclusions and exceptions including American Indian/Alaska Native status, former foster youth, inmates, medical conditions, caregivers, rehabilitation programs, TANF/SNAP workers, pregnant/postpartum women, and veterans with 100% disability.
Removed specific guidance on exceptions and short-term hardships such as inpatient services, disaster declarations, high unemployment counties, and medical travel requirements.
Removed detailed retroactive coverage changes including timelines for Medicaid Expansion (3 to 1 month) and other groups (3 to 2 months) effective January 1, 2027.
Removed specific reporting requirements for changes in citizenship, household composition, income, employment, and education status.
Removed detailed notice information about eligibility decisions and noncompliance with community engagement requirements.
Removed multiple webinar links and slides from September 10, 2026, June 30, 2026, May 21, 2026, and May 13, 2026 events.
Removed specific form references including Appendix A and B for community engagement reporting and exclusions, Medically Frail Guidance, and Presumptive Eligibility materials.
